mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below trend indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < trend for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% alongside a concurrent drop in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average signals a contraction in economic activity, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of triggered contractionary episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 1% in one month AND UNRATE > 6%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered emergency easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately driving higher inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a synchronized demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered expansionary episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for six consecutive months, coupled with a federal funds rate below the inflation rate, signals a loss of central bank credibility and rising real rates, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% for 6 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < CPIAUCSL
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly below zero in at least 60% of triggered high-inflation episodes.
